# When task-space control only needs classical Jdot*qdot, how can the original thread avoid explicitly constructing Jdot?

> **Current answer:** Maintainers recommend using forwardKinematics(model, data, q, v, 0*v) to zero out the generalized acceleration, then directly read the frame's classical acceleration drift using getFrameClassicalAcceleration(); the original author confirmed this is the classical Jdot*qdot required in the formula. It only returns the product/drift term, not the full Jdot matrix. Subsequent users' matrix formulas without official confirmation should not be included in this closed-loop experience.

## Key terms

- Classical point acceleration (经典点加速度)
- Spatial acceleration (空间加速度)
- Jacobian time derivative (雅可比时间导数)
- Acceleration drift term (加速度漂移项)
- Task-space control (任务空间控制)

## Problem and symptoms

- When only the product term of classical Jdot*qdot is needed, is explicit calculation of the classical Jacobian time derivative necessary?
- getFrameJacobianTimeVariation returns spatial acceleration-related quantities, but the controller formula qddot_des = pinv(J)(ac_des - Jdot*qdot) requires the classical acceleration drift.

## Environment

- 2021 Pinocchio API, two-degree-of-freedom arm example; original post lacks version, OS, or complete code.

## Priority diagnostics

- First confirm whether the controller needs full Jdot or just the product term of Jdot*qdot.
- Zero out qddot and run forward kinematics to make the frame's classical acceleration correspond to the velocity drift term.

## Possible causes

- The issue arises from mixing spatial Jacobian derivative with classical point acceleration control formulas.

## Attempts

- Maintainers recommend calling forwardKinematics(model, data, q, v, 0*v) and then directly obtaining the acceleration drift from getFrameClassicalAcceleration(), pointing to the corresponding controller in TSID.
- The original author confirmed that getFrameClassicalAcceleration() can directly provide the required classical Jdot*qdot.

## Effective fixes

- When only the product term is needed, call forwardKinematics with zero qddot and use getFrameClassicalAcceleration() to read the frame's classical acceleration drift, avoiding explicit construction of Jdot.

## Result

- The original author confirmed understanding and adoption of this approach; maintainers confirm it is simple and efficient.
